tools.name: Mem0

comparisons.title: Mem0 vs Zep: two different memory layers
comparisons.summary: Mem0 is a memory component you add to your app. Zep is an enterprise context layer for agents. Which one you want depends on whether you need "remember the preference" or "governed access to knowledge".

dimensions.name: Positioning
dimensions.a: Memory component: extracts facts and retrieves them with several signals
dimensions.b: Enterprise context layer: Context Lake plus Agent Skills

dimensions.a: Apache-2.0 SDK, with self-hosted and cloud tiers
dimensions.b: The repository holds Zep Cloud examples and integrations, not the product

dimensions.name: Algorithm
dimensions.a: Single-pass ADD-only extraction: memories accumulate and are never overwritten
dimensions.b: Governed context graphs, with repeated agent tasks distilled into skills

dimensions.name: Integration
dimensions.a: SDK or self-hosted service
dimensions.b: MCP or the official SDKs, with a Zep Cloud account

chooseA: You have one application and only want it to remember user preferences and state across sessions
You can accept append-only memories that rely on retrieval ranking to surface what is currently true
You want to self-host rather than put memory in someone else's managed service
chooseB: You need business data unified into governed context graphs that several agents share
You want the tasks agents repeat to accumulate into reusable skills
You accept using a managed service
comparisons.neither: If all you need is "let the chat assistant remember me", check whether your host tool already has memory built in — neither of these is needed.

comparisons.title: Mem0 vs OpenViking: extracted facts or context read on demand
comparisons.summary: Mem0 turns conversations into facts and retrieves them. OpenViking puts knowledge, memory and skills into one filesystem where agents go deeper by directory and summary as needed.

dimensions.name: Storage shape
dimensions.a: Extracted facts with vector retrieval
dimensions.b: A unified context database (directory + summary + semantics)

dimensions.name: How you use it
dimensions.a: SDK plugged into an existing application
dimensions.b: A context storage layer for agents

dimensions.name: Licence
dimensions.a: Apache-2.0
dimensions.b: AGPL-3.0

dimensions.name: Scale fit
dimensions.a: Small to medium sets of preference-type facts
dimensions.b: Long, hierarchically structured material

chooseA: What you need to remember is flat facts such as user preferences and settings
You do not want to take on the obligations of AGPL
You need a memory component that drops into an existing application
chooseB: Your material is inherently hierarchical (directories, modules, chapters) and suits organisation by directory
You want agents to read summaries first and drill into the source only when needed
You can accept the propagation obligations of AGPL-3.0
comparisons.neither: If context length is not the bottleneck, an ordinary vector store plus retrieval covers it; both of these are heavier.
